taxonomy.subtopic: Estrogen-induced thyroxine-binding globulin elevation and total hormone increase

questions.stem_html: A healthy woman at 14 weeks of gestation has no symptoms of thyroid disease. Testing shows an elevated total thyroxine concentration, a free thyroxine concentration within the pregnancy-adjusted reference range, and an appropriate thyrotropin concentration. The accompanying panel depicts this pattern. Which mechanism best explains the elevated total thyroxine?

options.text_html: Estrogen increases circulating thyroxine-binding globulin, transiently lowering free hormone and stimulating production until a new equilibrium with higher total hormone is reached
Human chorionic gonadotropin permanently blocks the thyrotropin receptor and prevents thyroid hormone synthesis
Pregnancy reduces hepatic synthesis of binding proteins, leaving more hormone unbound
Placental deiodinase completely prevents conversion of thyroxine to triiodothyronine in maternal tissues
Increased renal iodine clearance directly raises the fraction of unbound thyroxine

questions.explanation_html: Estrogen increases thyroxine-binding globulin production and reduces its clearance. More hormone becomes protein-bound, producing a transient fall in free hormone that stimulates additional thyroid hormone synthesis. A new euthyroid steady state is established with increased total T4 and T3 while free hormone remains approximately within gestational reference limits. Early pregnancy hCG can modestly lower TSH but does not explain the sustained rise in total T4.

wrong_choice_explanations.2: hCG weakly stimulates rather than permanently blocks the TSH receptor.
wrong_choice_explanations.4: Placental deiodinases regulate local metabolism but do not completely prevent maternal T4-to-T3 conversion.
wrong_choice_explanations.5: Higher iodine requirements do not directly increase the free fraction of T4.

questions.educational_objective: Estrogen-induced elevation of thyroxine-binding globulin raises total thyroid hormone during pregnancy while the active free fraction remains near the gestational reference range.
